intro: Picture this: a small colonial-style house with a koi pond in the middle of the garden, a pool to slip into for a quiet swim, and Bang Saray beach a short walk away — Baan Pimpisa Bangsaray Boutique Residence is a 3-star, 16-room boutique residence in the Bang Saray area of Bang Saray subdistrict, Sattahip district, Chonburi province, the southern Pattaya zone that still holds onto its fishing-village feel · open since 2015, it is a place that real reviews praise for its calm, its cleanliness, and its warm staff · there are two pools, a koi pond, a BBQ corner, bikes to borrow, and free parking · from about THB 1,100/night, rated around 8.8 from reviews on Trip.com

body.html: Who Baan Pimpisa is for — in the shortest possible summary, Baan Pimpisa Bangsaray Boutique Residence is a place for people who want to come to Pattaya but don't want to deal with the chaos of the city center · it isn't a high-rise hotel next to Walking Street, nor a big resort with an infinity pool and a fancy lobby · instead it's a small boutique residence of just 16 rooms in the Bang Saray area, a seaside community in southern Pattaya within Sattahip district, Chonburi province, that still keeps the air of a fishing village and a sense of simplicity · the building is a warm-toned colonial style, with a garden, a koi pond, and a pool that make it feel more like staying at a relative's house than checking into a hotel · it has been open since 2015 and is still going strong today, scoring well among places to stay in the Bang Saray area · real reviews line up on the same point: the people who suit this place are couples who want a quiet setting, small families bringing older relatives or children for an easygoing break, and travelers who are tired of the crowds and would rather fall asleep to the sound of the waves than music from a bar · as for anyone chasing nightlife, a convenience store on every corner, or large luxurious rooms, this may not be the answer, and you should look at hotels in central or south Pattaya instead · you could say Baan Pimpisa plays the "calm by the sea on an affordable budget" angle pretty clearly, and that's a stance you don't find often in a Pattaya zone that mostly sells buzz

Location and getting around — Baan Pimpisa sits in Moo 4, Bang Saray subdistrict, Sattahip district, on a quiet residential lane, about 400 meters from the Bang Saray fishing pier and a short walk to Bang Saray beach, roughly five to ten minutes · Bang Saray is a beach that local Thais and families favor more than foreign tourists, so the atmosphere is friendlier and clearly calmer than Pattaya or Jomtien beach, with plenty of fresh seafood restaurants along the shore at reasonable prices · distances run a little longer here: driving from the property to central Pattaya and Walking Street takes about 25–35 minutes depending on traffic · Cartoon Network Amazone and Ramayana Water Park are within a ten-minute drive, as are Nong Nooch Garden and the Pattaya Floating Market in the nearby radius · U-Tapao Airport (UTP) is about 25 km away, or roughly a 30 min drive, which is very convenient for anyone flying straight into U-Tapao · the honest caveat is that the Bang Saray area is most convenient with your own car or a rental, because public transport and the songthaews (red trucks) aren't as dense as in central Pattaya, so without a car you'll rely on Grab or taxis, which can be hard to hail at times, and fares into town add up quite a bit — this is something to weigh before you book

"We came here specifically to escape the chaos of Pattaya. We'd get up early, walk to Bang Saray beach, eat fresh seafood, then come back and sit by the pool. The staff are lovely and look after you like family · if you like peace and quiet, this is the place."

Room types and decor — with just 16 rooms, Baan Pimpisa is a small place that gets thorough attention · the main room is the Superior Room, with a queen or twin beds and a window to let in light · some rooms have a balcony or terrace looking out over the garden and pool, a feature many reviews say makes them feel especially relaxed · the decor leans into a warm holiday-home feel, using soft tones and woodwork; it isn't five-star luxurious but it's clean and tidy · in-room amenities include air conditioning, a fridge, cable TV, a safe, and drinking water, plus free Wi-Fi · many voices in the reviews agree that the rooms are very clean, the beds comfortable, and it's quiet enough to sleep soundly, a strength guests bring up often · but to be straight with you, there are caveats worth knowing: the rooms here aren't large and suit a relaxing stay for two more than a big group · some reviews note that certain rooms don't have a kettle for tea/coffee, so you'll need to bring your own or order extra · and the building has stairs and no elevator, so anyone with heavy luggage or who struggles with stairs should request a ground-floor room when booking · overall, the rooms at Baan Pimpisa are "just right" for relaxing; they don't sell space or luxury, but cleanliness and calm

Facilities, pools, and garden — even as a small property, Baan Pimpisa packs in facilities that are charming for its size · the highlight is two swimming pools (indoor and outdoor) plus a kids' pool, which many reviews describe as small but clean and quiet, better for a relaxing soak than serious lap swimming · another thing that gives the place its own charm is the koi pond in the middle of the garden, which many people mention as making the setting shady and calm, perfect for sipping morning coffee or letting the kids watch the fish · there's also a BBQ corner for anyone who wants to grill in a small group, bicycle hire for rides around the Bang Saray area that fits the seaside-village mood nicely, free private parking, luggage storage, and free Wi-Fi throughout · to be honest, the facilities here are the "small but complete for relaxing" kind; there's no big fitness center, full spa, or multiple dining zones like a large resort · but for people who come intending to sleep quietly, take a dip, and head out for seafood by the beach, what's on offer is enough and a good fit for a slow-paced break

Food and dining nearby — one thing to know before booking is that Baan Pimpisa doesn't include breakfast in the standard room rate; breakfast is available for an extra charge if you want it · this is normal for small boutique stays in this area, and honestly it isn't a big problem, because Bang Saray's strength is its fresh seafood restaurants by the beach, within a walk or a short drive of the property · many reviews speak well of the food and drinks from the property itself, especially people who order in the garden corner or by the pool, who say the flavors are good and the setting is nice · for main meals, most guests choose to go out for seafood at the restaurants along Bang Saray beach, known for fresh produce and friendlier prices than restaurants in central Pattaya · markets and convenience stores in the Bang Saray area are decent but not on every corner the way they are in town, so if you want late-night snacks or specific items, stock up during the day · overall, food at Baan Pimpisa isn't the main reason to come and eat on site; it's a nicely done extra, while the real star is the Bang Saray area seafood all around

Service — this is where Baan Pimpisa earns its most solid and consistent praise · because it's a small place run by the owner and team, many real reviews talk about warm, friendly staff who care for you like a relative coming to stay · many recount how the team helped recommend seafood restaurants in the area, helped with getting around, and looked after the little details better than the price would suggest · being a small property turns into an advantage here: guests don't wait in long queues and get more personal attention than at a big hotel · the caveat to understand is that, given its small size and format, some things a big hotel offers — like 24-hour room service or a full tour desk — may not be as complete, but what you get is sincerity and closeness, which is exactly what people choosing this kind of boutique are looking for anyway

What real reviews say (praise and gripes) — pulling from Trip.com, TripAdvisor, and various booking platforms, the picture is fairly consistent · on the praise side: a genuinely quiet setting that escapes the Pattaya chaos, the cleanliness of the rooms and shared spaces, warm and friendly staff who pay attention, the koi pond and shady garden, a small but clean pool, being near Bang Saray beach and fresh seafood restaurants, and good value for the price · many people use the words "best value" and "refreshing and relaxing" · on the gripe side: the things that come up are the rooms not being large and the soundproofing between rooms and from the pool area, which some reviews say lets in noise from the next room or from people using the pool at certain times · next is the building having stairs and no elevator, which makes things a little awkward for anyone with heavy luggage, plus some rooms lacking a kettle for tea/coffee, and a location that relies on a private car if you want to head into central Pattaya often · most of these gripes are manageable by setting the right expectation: this is a small beachside boutique that sells calm, not an in-town hotel that sells completeness and convenience on every front

"Clean rooms, lovely staff, a small but crystal-clear pool, and a beautiful koi pond that's relaxing to watch · the only gripe is that the soundproofing between rooms isn't great, and at night you hear a bit from the next room. Next time I'll ask for a corner room instead."

Price and value — the starting rate for a Superior Room is about THB 1,100/night in the normal range, climbing to roughly THB 1,400–1,800 over long weekends or high season · compared with beachside stays in the Pattaya zone in general, this price counts as accessible and great value among boutiques that sell a quiet setting, especially once you factor in the two pools, the koi-pond garden, free parking, and warm, easygoing service · stays in the Bang Saray area that are right on the sea at this price point rarely have a pool or garden this nice, while big beachfront hotels in central Pattaya jump up another level in price · if you plan a slow-paced break, using the property as a base to walk the beach, eat seafood, and chill by the pool, the money you put toward Baan Pimpisa buys back calm and atmosphere in full · but if the main goal is a night out in central Pattaya every day, the accumulating travel costs into town may eat into the value, so weigh it against your own style of trip

What to know before booking — a few things help make the stay smoother · one, this is a small property of just 16 rooms and popular with couples, so it fills up fast on long weekends — book ahead · two, if you're sensitive to noise, ask for a corner room or one that isn't right next to the pool or too close to the neighboring room, since reviews mention soundproofing a bit · three, the building has stairs and no elevator, so if you have heavy luggage, are bringing older travelers, or struggle with stairs, request a ground-floor room when booking · four, breakfast isn't included in the standard rate, so plan your morning meal ahead or ask about the extra breakfast charge when booking · five, the Bang Saray location is most convenient with your own car or a rental; without a car, allow for the cost and time of hailing a Grab into town · six, since it's a small property that may not be on every booking platform with the same room count, compare prices and check the booking/cancellation terms on each channel before you hit book

Summary — from all the real reviews, Baan Pimpisa Bangsaray Boutique Residence is the best fit for people who want Pattaya in its quiet version, a seaside break in Bang Saray on an affordable budget · the cleanliness, staff who are warm like they're welcoming a relative, two pools, a koi-pond garden, and a location within walking distance of Bang Saray beach and fresh seafood make it worthwhile in a way that's hard to find in a Pattaya zone that mostly sells buzz · if you're after nightlife, in-town convenience on every corner, or large luxurious rooms, this may not be the answer, and you should consider hotels in central or south Pattaya instead · but for a relaxing trip where you want to sleep to the quiet, wake up and walk the beach, and use the property as a small home by the sea — Baan Pimpisa is a choice that meets that need charmingly and affordably, and it's the reason many guests say they'll come back again

faq.q: Where is Baan Pimpisa Bangsaray · is it far from central Pattaya?
faq.a: The property is in Moo 4, Bang Saray subdistrict, Sattahip district, Chonburi province, in the southern Pattaya zone · it's about 400 meters from the Bang Saray fishing pier and a short walk to Bang Saray beach · from central Pattaya and Walking Street it's about a 25–35 minute drive, and it's roughly a 30 min drive from U-Tapao Airport

It's a great fit for couples, small families, and anyone who wants a quiet break by the sea in Bang Saray, escaping the bustle of central Pattaya · it has two pools, a koi-pond garden, and warm service · if you're focused on a night out in central Pattaya every day or want a large luxurious room, a hotel in central/south Pattaya may suit you better

faq.q: What does Baan Pimpisa cost to start · what room types are there?
faq.a: Prices start at about THB 1,100/night for a Superior Room in the normal range · there are queen-bed and twin-bed rooms, and some rooms have a balcony/terrace looking over the garden and pool · long-weekend prices climb to roughly THB 1,400–1,800, so book ahead and compare across platforms

faq.q: Does Baan Pimpisa have breakfast and a pool?
faq.a: There are two swimming pools (indoor and outdoor) plus a kids' pool and a koi pond in the middle of the garden · as for breakfast, it's not included in the standard room rate but is available for an extra charge · the area's strength is the fresh seafood restaurants along Bang Saray beach, within a walk or short drive

faq.q: What are noise and convenience like at Baan Pimpisa?
faq.a: Many reviews praise the quiet of the Bang Saray area, but there's a caveat about soundproofing between rooms and from the pool area being so-so at times · the building has stairs and no elevator · if you're a light sleeper or have heavy luggage, we suggest asking for a corner room and a ground-floor room when booking

faq.q: Do you need a private car to get to Baan Pimpisa?
faq.a: You don't have to have one, but a private car or rental is most convenient, because public transport in the Bang Saray area isn't as dense as in central Pattaya · the property has free parking and bikes to borrow · without a car you'll rely on Grab or taxis, so allow extra time and cost when heading into town
